title: Mom gave him three days; a friend in a supercar scaled it
description: Nate blows his mom's money on bad trades, gets three days to win it back and is thrown out. A friend in a red supercar runs over his chart printouts, takes his laptop and they grind his fomo account up to six figures, so when Mom pulls up beside them at a red light Nate tells her 'We scaled it.' Unlike the stepmom version, here the rescuer arrives already rich in a supercar and takes over the laptop, and the two ride to the payoff together.
text:
SCENE 1 — INT. NATE'S BEDROOM — EVENING
Nate's mom looms over him on his bed, crumpled chart printouts all over the duvet, a wall of taped-up charts and glowing monitors behind.
MOM: Nate! Where did all my money go? You spent it on these?
She lifts a grey storage bin over her head and dumps a cascade of chart printouts onto the bed.
MOM: How many did you buy?
NATE: Not that many.
She grabs his phone off the pile and shoves it at him.
★ fomo screen: Token chart down — on Nate's phone in her hand, the line sliding red
MOM: You used my money for this?
NATE: I'm trading them.
MOM: Your room looks like a trading floor.
NATE: Exactly, bad example.
She slams the empty bin down in front of him and wags her finger.
MOM: Three days.
NATE: What?
MOM: Win it back.
MOM: Or you're out.
MOM: Three days.
NATE: Mom!
SCENE 2 — MONTAGE — NATE'S ROOM — DAYS AND NIGHTS
Cool morning light: Nate at his desk, wiping his phone screen and lining up charts.
Golden hour through the window behind him: he polishes the screen with a cloth and taps into a trade.
★ fomo screen: Token chart down — on Nate's phone, the line going nowhere
Nate sits back and stares flatly at camera.
NATE: Nothing.
NATE: Better charts.
Nate under a ring light in front of a wall of extra monitors, squinting at the lines.
Locked-off wide: Nate on an office chair in his room, phone in hand; the window jumps from day to sunset to night and back while the piles of printouts grow around him.
NATE: Soon.
NATE: Zero.
NATE: Come on.
NATE: No.
NATE: One.
NATE: Just one.
Nate sits buried between two mountains of printouts.
★ fomo screen: Token chart up — on Nate's phone, one small green candle
Nate jumps out of his chair.
NATE: Yes!
NATE: I can fix it.
Mom bursts in and stuffs his clothes into a duffel bag.
MOM: Out!
MOM: I gave you three days.
MOM: Pack!
NATE: Mom!
SCENE 3 — EXT. FRONT DOOR — DUSK
Mom stands in the lit doorway; Nate on the step with a suitcase, his printouts dumped on the lawn.
MOM: You made your choice.
The door shuts. Nate stands alone with the heap.
NATE: Bro, these things ruined my life.
SCENE 4 — EXT. DRIVEWAY — GOLDEN HOUR
Nate crouches in the driveway, digging through a tub of crumpled printouts, and hears an engine.
NATE: Wait.
A red supercar's wheel rolls over a fallen printout, crushing it into the asphalt.
Nate's face in extreme close-up, screaming in cartoon horror.
NATE: Ah! Bro!
The scissor door swings up; his friend climbs out, unbothered.
FRIEND: Why are you trading these?
NATE (O.S.): I got kicked out over these.
Two-shot by the tub and the bin bags, the garage door behind.
NATE: It's not funny.
FRIEND: It's a little funny.
NATE: You just ran over one.
FRIEND: You weren't selling it anyway.
FRIEND: Bro, how are you trading these?
NATE: I buy them.
FRIEND: And?
NATE: And they go up.
FRIEND: Clearly.
FRIEND: Give me your laptop.
FRIEND: Watch.
SCENE 5 — MONTAGE — FOLDING TABLE IN THE DRIVEWAY — DAY TO NIGHT TO DAY
His friend flips open Nate's laptop on a folding table; Nate leans in beside him, sceptical.
★ fomo screen: Desktop trading — on Nate's laptop as his friend's hands fly over the keys
NATE: Dude!
Dusk, laptop glow on both faces: his friend walks Nate through a trade and Nate takes it himself; the position reads +$64 (+3.2%).
Night under the porch light: Nate rubs his eyes, still clicking, moths around the lamp; the balance reads $1,480.
A small win: Nate's tiny fist pump, his friend nods without looking up; the balance reads $9,700.
Next morning, a bigger win: Nate grips his phone, eyes wide.
★ fomo screen: Token chart up — on Nate's phone, the position reads +$24,600
NATE: Bro, what do you do?
FRIEND: I told you. I scale accounts.
NATE: Scale it.
FRIEND: Say less.
Nate's phone blows up in his hand.
★ fomo screen: Home (rich) — on Nate's phone, the balance reads $640,000
NATE: Bro!
Crash zoom into Nate's screaming mouth, to black.
SCENE 6 — EXT. CITY STREET — GOLDEN HOUR
The red supercar pulls away down a brick-lined street, exhaust popping flames, Nate in the passenger seat; pedestrians turn to stare.
Through the passenger window: Nate grinning, his friend at the wheel.
NATE: Bro, this thing is insane.
At a red light the supercar stops beside a dented beige sedan; Mom stares across from behind its wheel.
MOM: Nate? Is that you?
MOM: How did you even make it?
Nate glances at her with a smug side look.
NATE: We scaled it.
Nate turns to camera, holding up his phone.
★ fomo screen: Home (rich) — on Nate's phone held to camera, the balance reads $640,000
NATE: Want to trade like me? Download fomo through the link in my bio.

cast.description: Teen, slim; big glossy brown eyes, thick dark brows, dark curly hair; navy cap worn backwards, plain white tee, thin silver chain, black pants, white sneakers. Same look in the supercar.
Early 40s, glamorous; long wavy chestnut hair; white crop tank top, plain black bike shorts. Big exasperated gestures, finger-wagging.

Early 20s, relaxed and confident; short dark hair in a fade, light stubble; black bomber jacket over a plain white tee, heavy gold chain, grey sweatpants, white sneakers. Drives a red supercar with scissor doors. Cool half-smile.
